The function $f(x)$ is represented by the mapping diagram above. What is ${f}^{-1}(1)?$
question.worked_solution:
**Method 1**

The function ${f}^{-1}(x)$ reverses the action of $f(x),$ as depicted below. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14208916/assets/17b769a94abc2035d5d24e82c65d9c8fd6252152482826c3a34e8708d246c213.png)

 

From the above, we see that ${f}^{-1}(1)=-2.$

**Method 2**

From the given mapping diagram, we have:

$$
f(-2)=1
$$

Applying ${f}^{-1}$ to both sides of the above equation, and using the fact that ${f}^{-1}(f(x))=x,$ we get:

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{-1}(f(-2)) & ={f}^{-1}(1) \\ -2 & ={f}^{-1}(1)\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we conclude that ${f}^{-1}(1)=-2.$
